title: Windows credential-lifecycle forensics, exact-SHA CI closure and release handoff

credential_failure_forensics.source_of_evidence: GitHub Actions check-run annotations for the Windows release validation run on the M42 tip, plus a local reproduction that forces the legacy default text encoding
credential_failure_forensics.reproduction_command: env -u LANG -u LC_CTYPE PYTHONUTF8=0 PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0 LC_ALL=C python -m pytest -o addopts= -q tests/test_credential_lifecycle.py tests/test_ddr_forensic_regressions.py
credential_failure_forensics.root_cause: static Windows-suite tests called Path.read_text() without an explicit encoding, so the runner decoded UTF-8 repository source (Persian UI strings) with the platform default codepage and raised UnicodeDecodeError before any credential behaviour executed
credential_failure_forensics.corrective_change: every repository-source read in the Windows suite states encoding='utf-8'; verify_release.py and the packaging tools do the same

packaging_stage_forensics.corrective_change: publish release_dir before building; Start-Transcript the whole step and stop it before annotating; wrap the step in try/catch/finally that emits one bounded, redacted ::error annotation through packaging/junit_report.py --annotate over the transcript, pip-install.log and pyinstaller-build.log and re-throws; capture pip install and pip check into pip-install.log with a bounded tail inside the thrown message; resolve the release output directory and its emptiness guard before any log is written; add -PythonExe with an explicit minor-version assertion; scope ErrorActionPreference to the redirected native pipelines and clear PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference; record the runner volume's free bytes so an out-of-space packaging environment is visible; requirements-build.txt now pins pefile==2023.2.7, the newest release satisfying pyinstaller 6.11.1's >=2022.5.30,!=2024.8.26 constraint, which ships a py3-none-any wheel so the build machine needs no compiler
packaging_stage_forensics.exception: Locked dependency installation failed - pip: ERROR: Cannot install -r requirements-build.txt (line 3) and pefile==2024.8.26 because these package versions have conflicting dependencies; pyinstaller 6.11.1 depends on pefile!=2024.8.26 and >=2022.5.30; sys_platform == "win32"; ERROR: ResolutionImpossible
packaging_stage_forensics.phase: packaging environment preparation, after the Windows regression suite and before bundle analysis
packaging_stage_forensics.reproduction: exact-SHA Windows gate runs for this branch: the run at f047dc70de5f00ff0948dbd8ea9735b80d853757 failed step 7 with only 'Process completed with exit code 1'; the instrumented run at 54385f8f90b16bddaa64f7cfe03ac1fc41f78b70 published the stage name in a ::error annotation
packaging_stage_forensics.root_cause_detail: four harness defects are proven from source and evidence: (1) release_dir job output was set only at the end of the step, so the always() artifact upload contained nothing when the build failed; (2) no failure annotation or step-summary entry was emitted, so the failing stage was unrecoverable once the log endpoint was unreachable; (3) the step selected the interpreter with the Windows 'py' launcher, which resolves registry-registered runtimes rather than the Actions tool-cache Python the job provisioned and tested with; (4) build_windows.ps1 runs under ErrorActionPreference=Stop while redirecting native stderr (2>&1 | Tee-Object), the documented pattern that turns PyInstaller's progress log - or a thrown inner-script error - into a terminating NativeCommandError or a swallowed non-terminating error. The specific stage that failed at f047dc7 is recorded as UNRESOLVED_PENDING_INSTRUMENTED_RUN; the instrumented gate is the evidence source, not this file.
packaging_stage_forensics.test: step 7 'Build portable bundle and installer; run frozen executable smoke' (steps 1-6, including the 26-module Windows regression suite, conclude success at both SHAs)
packaging_stage_forensics.traceback: no traceback - the pre-instrumentation step wrote nothing to the error stream, and at the instrumented run the transcript tail contained only the Start-Transcript header because the annotation was emitted while the transcript was still open
packaging_stage_forensics.failing_stage: pip install -r requirements-lock.txt -r requirements-build.txt into the fresh .windows-build-venv returned non-zero; PyInstaller never started (the annotation reported 'pyinstaller-build.log: not found')

ruled_out.hypothesis: the pinned requirements have no Windows cp312 wheel and pip must compile them
ruled_out.evidence: pip download --only-binary=:all: --platform win_amd64 --python-version 3.12 --implementation cp --abi cp312 -r requirements-lock.txt -r requirements-build.txt resolved and saved all 31 pins plus transitive deps (bcrypt/PyMuPDF/PySide6/shiboken6 via cp39-abi3-win_amd64, pyinstaller via py3-none-win_amd64)

ruled_out.hypothesis: the py launcher cannot see the Actions tool-cache interpreter, so the build venv is never created
ruled_out.evidence: the annotation reports 'Build interpreter: C:\hostedtoolcache\windows\Python\3.12.10\x64\python.exe' and virtualenv creation succeeded before the dependency stage; the -PythonExe change removed the launcher dependency entirely

ruled_out.hypothesis: the release build refuses to start because the checkout is dirty after the test suite
ruled_out.evidence: the guard throws 'Refusing release build from a dirty worktree' with a distinct message, and the pytest outputs (.pytest_cache/, __pycache__/, *.log, release/) are git-ignored

ruled_out.hypothesis: the encoding-defect class from the earlier run is still failing tests
ruled_out.evidence: step 6 concluded success at both SHAs with zero failure annotations

packaging_stage_forensics.stage_mechanism: requirements-build.txt pinned pefile==2024.8.26, the exact version PyInstaller 6.11.1 excludes on Windows.  The exclusion is guarded by a sys_platform == "win32" marker, so the conflict exists only in a Windows resolve: pip installs the same two files cleanly on Linux and the pin was therefore never contradicted by any Linux evidence.

corrections.superseded_claim: the entry previously recorded under ruled_out claimed the requirement files were consistent because pip install -r requirements-lock.txt -r requirements-build.txt plus pip check succeeded in a fresh Linux venv
corrections.why_wrong: that evidence cannot observe the defect: the conflicting PyInstaller requirement is guarded by a sys_platform == "win32" marker, so a Linux resolve is always clean.  The Linux check was kept as evidence that no non-marked conflict exists, and its conclusion of overall consistency was withdrawn
corrections.corrected_method: evaluate every pinned dependency edge under a Windows marker environment (sys_platform=win32, platform_system=Windows, os_name=nt, platform_machine=AMD64) against the repository pins - 33 win32-applicable edges over 31 pins, now reporting no conflict - and lock that invariant in tests/test_windows_release_gate_contract.py without needing network access

internal_gates.requirement: success on the exact final SHA for Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13, including exact-source, locked dependency, test and wheel verification

success on the exact final SHA for the Windows regression suite, the PyInstaller portable bundle, the frozen executable smoke run, Inno Setup installer compilation, artifact SHA-256 verification, release metadata and acceptance-report generation

gate_result_policy: A commit cannot contain the identity of the run that validates it. Run IDs, conclusions, test counts and artifact digests are recorded in the mission report and in the runtime-generated acceptance-report.json artifact, never in committed source.

preserved_boundaries.engineering_scope: M41 boundaries retained; no standards-compliance claim is added by this checkpoint
